newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress withdraws support for gov't - UNI. [CORRECTED]
newsitem.headline: India Congress withdraws support for gov't - UNI. [CORRECTED]

text.p: India's Congress Party has decided to withdraw support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition government, the United News of India (UNI) news agency said on Sunday. (Corrects news agency from Press Trust of India).
It said Congress president Sitaram Kesri met India's President Shankar Dayal Sharma on Sunday morning and handed over a letter listing the grounds for the withdrawal of support.
It was not immediately clear if the Congress decision meant the shaky nine-month-old government led by Deve Gowda would have to resign and call a snap mid-term national election.
Deve Gowda's minority United Front alliance controls some 178 deputies in the 545-member Lok Sabha or lower house. The Congress has 142 deputies.

Asked to confirm the news agency report that the Congress had decided to withdraw support to Deve Gowda's nine-month-old government, Kesri told Reuters: "Yes. It has been done." He refused to elaborate.
A Congress spokesman said the party had called a news conference at 4:00 p.m. (1030 GMT).
